covalent.note: Covalent radius; PubChem's values are those of Cordero et al., Dalton Trans. 2008, 2832.

vdw.note: Van der Waals radius (Los Alamos National Laboratory).

allen.note: Configuration energy (Allen electronegativity) in eV, not converted to the Pauling-like scale; Mann 2000a.

polarizability.note: Recommended value of the 2018 table: from experiment where it is precise enough, otherwise from high-level calculation.

crust.note: Jefferson Lab estimate for Earth's crust, via PubChem ('8.23×10⁴ milligrams per kilogram').

ocean.note: Jefferson Lab estimate for sea water, via PubChem ('2×10⁻³ milligrams per liter').

solar.note: Proto-solar (4.567 Ga ago) elemental mass fraction, column 'Elemental Mass Fractions' of ESM Table A13; the table gives no uncertainty (relative sigma of N(E) in Table 6 applies).

solarLogEps.note: A(E) = log10(N_E/N_H) + 12, 'Solar System Present' log (E/H)+12; basis: average of solar and meteoritic values; unc = 1 sigma in dex as printed.

body.note: In a 70 kg reference adult (ICRP Publication 23, 1975, Table 110).

crystal.reference: Straumanis, M. E. (1949). Journal of Applied Physics 20, 726.
crystal.note: Measured at 25 °C. The original paper reported kX units; COD multiplied the cell constant by 1.00202 to give ångström (note in CIF).

tonnesPerYear.note: World primary smelter production, aluminium metal, 2025 (USGS: 74,000 thousand metric tons).

unitValue.note: Price, ingot, average U.S. market (spot), cents per pound [Aluminum], 2025; per kg of the material named, as USGS gives it.

critical.note: Ore (bauxite), intermediate (alumina) and metal (aluminium) listed as one entry; aluminium is named, so the mapping is direct.

origin.note: Read off Fig. 39 at the dotted 'age of the Sun' line (t = 9.2 Gyr after the Big Bang, 4.6 Gyr ago): pixel fractions of the stacked areas (agb 0.109, massive_stars 0.891); quantised to 0.05. Stack height 71 px. Paper: 'For the elements from Ne to Ge, the newly synthesized amounts are very small for AGB stars, and the small green areas are mostly for mass loss.'

splitting.note: Atomic-beam measurement (Harvey, Evans and Lew 1972), as tabulated in arXiv:2511.08881 Table I. Splitting derived as 3A.

siHistory.text: 27Al+ (1121 THz) is a secondary representation of the second.

plantRole.text: At low concentrations it stimulates growth in some species, such as tea; in acid soils dissolved aluminium is instead a major cause of poor root growth.

humanRole.text: No known role in the body.

history.nameOrigin: From alumina and alum (Latin alumen), the compounds in which the metal was first suspected.
history.note: PubChem lists the year as 'Ancient' because alum was used in antiquity; the metal itself was unknown before 1825. Lavoisier had suspected alumina to be the oxide of an unknown metal (1787).

prose.text: Aluminium is a light, silvery metal and the most abundant metal in Earth's crust; we meet it as drink cans, kitchen foil, window frames and aircraft skins. It looks reactive on paper, yet it barely corrodes, because a thin, transparent oxide film seals its surface within moments of exposure to air. Its radioactive isotope aluminium-26, with a half-life of about 717,000 years, was a major heat source that melted some of the first small planetary bodies of the young Solar System. The atom's single 3p electron ([Ne] 3s² 3p¹, ground term ²P°₁/₂) is easier to remove than magnesium's outer 3s electron: 578 kJ/mol against 738 kJ/mol.
